newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale proposes C$1.7 mln in malt barley research.
newsitem.headline: Goodale proposes C$1.7 mln in malt barley research.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Friday he plans to propose a C$1.7 million federal program to help the malt barley industry develop new seed varieties to remain competitive on world markets.
"I'll propose that the government of Canada contribute C$1.7 million to develop new varieties of malting barley," Goodale told delegates at the Canada Grains Council meeting.
The Canadian Wheat Board held a 48 percent share of the world malting barley market in the 1994/95 (Aug/July) marketing year, CWB figures show.

"The malting circumstances of malting barley are changing very rapidly over time. We've done well based on the varieties we have now but there is concern that the shelf life of the varieties we have at the moment is relatively short and we'd be well advised to develop and test market new varieties," he said.
